CONCEPT A — THE FOLD-OUT MENU THEATRE. Main composition is boldly asymmetric: left 38% holds a monumental two-line headline "Tu carta." / "En escena." in black geometric bold on warm ivory, with a small hand-drawn cobalt bracket connecting the text to the scene. Right 62% is an unexpected sculptural accordion of THREE tall cream menu panels opening toward the viewer on a saturated coral stepped plinth. Panels share a hinge/fold but look like a conceptual digital-menu presentation rather than a literal paper-only product. Left panel shows "Casa Naranja" then "Entrantes", middle "Platos", right "Postres". The front-most readable panel includes a visible black "Ver carta →" control. No invented dish prices or labels. Show only simple category motifs, limited clean text. A confident dark violet AUBERGINE character stands low foreground right, one cream hand pulling the accordion open. A mischievous slim cobalt FORK character leans down from an upper panel and holds a small illustrated ribbon; recognizable metal fork head rendered graphic, not robot. A tiny lemon wedge (without face) becomes a bright accent caught on the fold. The characters make the opening action readable. This is a fresh staging of the product. Saturated coral scene, vivid yellow fold edges and tiny cobalt details, plenty of warm ivory reading space. Unusual oblique viewpoint; panels stagger in depth, controlled warm contact shadows, strong modern product shot with flat illustrated actors. Fine sophisticated illustration, not childish mascots, not generic stock SaaS cards.
